symptom: A release branch cut from an older tag fails check:vocabularies because origin/main later removed a debt entry that never existed on the release branch.
direct_cause: resolveReferenceBaselines always added origin/main alongside HEAD^1 and merge-base, so a later main snapshot could impose a stricter debt cap on a divergent branch.
class_root: Historical ratchet reference selection did not guard the optional origin/main snapshot with the branch ancestry invariant.
affected_population: Release and hotfix branches cut before origin/main retired vocabulary debt
Any divergent branch whose baseline file differs from a newer origin/main snapshot
entry_points: run() resolves one historical baseline before evaluateHistoricalRatchet
resolveReferenceBaselines() selects explicit, main, merge-base, or parent history
internal_only_reason: The invariant is repository-specific Git history policy; no third-party API determines which branch snapshot is authoritative.

invariant_owner_layer.why: The resolver is the single enforcement owner for historical reference selection, and its topology tests exercise both divergent and ancestor histories.

invariants: The historical ratchet compares every available trusted historical snapshot.
origin/main is eligible only when it is an ancestor of HEAD.
A divergent branch still compares HEAD when dirty, HEAD^1, and merge-base, but never borrows a newer main-only snapshot.

door_reduction.why_not: The production resolver and its behavior tests remain separate doors: the resolver owns selection, while the test door proves branch topology with real Git fixtures. Combining them would remove executable regression evidence.

generality_proof: Every check:vocabularies invocation converges through resolveReferenceBaselines before historical evaluation. The ancestor predicate controls only the optional origin/main snapshot while the existing multi-snapshot ratchet remains active for release, hotfix, and ordinary task branches.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Collect the existing historical snapshots and admit origin/main only when ancestry proves it belongs to this branch history.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: run consumes the resolver result for every historical ratchet evaluation.
Real temporary Git repositories cover divergent release history and ancestor main history.

recurrence.reason: Any future release or hotfix cut before main debt cleanup can reproduce the same false failure.
same_class_scan: Temporary Git fixture with divergent release and main commits

prevention.invariant: Historical debt is evaluated against every available historical snapshot; origin/main is included only when it is an ancestor of HEAD.
prevention.failure_mode: If no readable trusted snapshot exists, the gate fails closed with a reference-unavailable error.
prevention.strategy: Keep the existing HEAD, HEAD^1, and merge-base collection order, and gate only the origin/main addition with merge-base --is-ancestor.

legacy_paths.rationale: The old unconditional origin/main addition is removed in the same change; the existing multi-snapshot history path remains.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The change uses the existing Git CLI and Node standard library; no third-party dependency controls the invariant.

migration: No stored vocabulary data changes. Existing VOCAB_BASE_REF and --reference-baseline overrides remain authoritative.
residual_risks: A repository with no merge-base, parent, or explicit reference still requires a deliberate baseline seed and remains fail-closed.
